title: Steady Rates, Familiar Debates
overview: A quiet news day on the ground in Türkiye: the central bank held its course, the lira stayed stable, and the big political story was less about policy than about optics in Ankara. Regionally, tensions simmer in the Gulf and Red Sea, but nothing directly disrupts travel or daily life here today.
body: The Central Bank kept its policy rate at 37% for a fifth consecutive meeting, matching analyst expectations. Bloomberg and ING both note the bank is balancing disinflation progress against oil-price risk, with most observers now pointing to October as the likely start of gradual easing. For residents, this means loan and mortgage costs stay high for now, but the lira held steady today at 48.51/USD and 56.44/EUR — no sudden swings to plan around. Separately, a report in Gazete Oksijen found the iPhone 17 (referred to as "iPhone Duo") costs 137% more in Turkey than in the US, a reminder that imported electronics carry a heavy import-tax premium here.
